question: Let \(c = \dfrac{2\pi}{11}.\) What is the value of \[\small \dfrac{\sin 3c \cdot \sin 6c \cdot \sin 9c \cdot \sin 12c \cdot \sin 15c}{\sin c \cdot \sin 2c \cdot \sin 3c \cdot \sin 4c \cdot \sin 5c}?\]
solution:
Because \(11c=2\pi\), shifting numerator angles by a full turn makes their sine values match the denominator factors, possibly with a minus sign.

Use
\[
\sin(\theta+2\pi)=\sin\theta,
\qquad
\sin(2\pi-\theta)=-\sin\theta.
\]
These identities give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sin12c&=\sin(c+2\pi)=\sin c,\\
\sin15c&=\sin(4c+2\pi)=\sin4c,\\
\sin6c&=\sin(2\pi-5c)=-\sin5c,\\
\sin9c&=\sin(2\pi-2c)=-\sin2c.
\end{aligned}
\]
The denominator angles \(c,2c,\ldots,5c\) all lie strictly between \(0\) and \(\pi\), so none of their sines is zero. Substitution now gives
\[
\frac{\sin3c\,(-\sin5c)\,(-\sin2c)\,\sin c\,\sin4c}
{\sin c\,\sin2c\,\sin3c\,\sin4c\,\sin5c}
=\boxed{1}.
\]
The two negative signs cancel, and the answer is choice \(\textbf{E}\).
